structuralFindings: ATR true range uses raw item.high/item.low, not the highs/lows arrays that elsewhere fall back to close.
In JavaScript arithmetic, null high/low is coerced to 0. With prevClose around 100, a null high or low can generate a true range near 100 rather than an unknown/fallback range.

Two null-H/L bars in a 20-bar window with otherwise 2-point ranges at close=100 produce deployed ATR%=11.8 and an upper-gate rejection; an explicit close-fallback diagnostic comparator is 1.8% and passes.
Undefined or invalid non-null high/low instead yields NaN range; average() filters nonfinite values, silently shrinking the effective ATR range denominator.
atr20=0 becomes atrPercent=null because of atr20&&close; deployed Formal then coerces null through (atrPercent||0) and rejects on the lower bound.
formal_gate_overlap_observer_v0_3 is therefore not exact for ATR missingness: it labels missing atrPercent UNKNOWN although deployed Formal rejects it.
counterevidenceAndLimits: The official historical request asks for high/low and normal market sessions are expected to supply them; no live-production frequency of missing H/L has yet been established.
A structural counterexample proves a correctness vulnerability, not that current candidate results have been affected.
ATR itself already has dedicated volatility/risk research; this artifact does not claim the 1%/10% thresholds are economically wrong.
Corporate-action raw/continuity semantics are a separate known source issue and are not re-litigated here.
